chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Do not receive (goods) before others (are able to), and do not buy what is received (before others), and do not eat from it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.تَلَقِّي: Receiving goods (specifically before others in a trade context)
key_terms.تُلُقِّيَ: What is received (passive participle referring to the goods)
key_terms.مِنْهَالٌ الْقَصَّابُ: Minhal al-Qassab, a narrator known as 'the butcher'

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on receiving goods outside the city before others?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the prohibition of 'iltiqaa', a pre-Islamic trade practice where a merchant would meet incoming caravans outside the city to buy goods at a lower price before they reached the main market. By forbidding the receipt, purchase, and consumption of such goods, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) ensures fair competition and prevents market manipulation, a ruling deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence to protect the economic interests of local merchants.
